title: How Blood Pressure Works
summary: Josh and Chuck open with news of Isaac Hayes's death, reportedly from a stroke linked to high blood pressure, and use it to launch a discussion of hypertension. They explain blood pressure as the force of blood against artery walls, define systolic (top number, optimal around 120) and diastolic (bottom number, around 80) readings, and cover pulse pressure (the difference between them) and its link to hardened vessels and an overly thick heart. They discuss accuracy problems with public blood pressure machines that need recalibration, white coat hypertension, blood pressure changes during pregnancy, prevalence statistics (about thirty percent of adults twenty and over, with poor people at higher rates), risk reduction through diet (the DASH diet), quitting smoking, limiting salt and alcohol, and the types of anti-hypertensive medications and their side effects. The episode closes with a sponsor break and a plug for a how stuff works article on frogs.

segments.title: Opening banter and Isaac Hayes news
segments.summary: Hosts open the show and Chuck shares the reported cause of death of soul singer Isaac Hayes, a stroke linked to high blood pressure. Josh says he has wanted to cover hypertension and mentions his EMT school experience.

segments.title: What blood pressure is and systolic pressure
segments.summary: Blood pressure is defined as the force of blood against artery walls. The top (systolic) number is explained, with an optimal reading around 120 for healthy adults.

segments.title: Measuring blood pressure and machine accuracy
segments.summary: Blood pressure cuffs are described as a noninvasive way to measure pressure. The hosts warn that public machines in drug stores may be inaccurate if not recalibrated, so readings should not drive medical decisions without a doctor.

segments.title: Diastolic and pulse pressure
segments.summary: Diastolic (bottom number), around 80 for healthy adults, is the pressure when the heart is at rest. Pulse pressure, the difference between systolic and diastolic, is discussed, with high values linked to hardened vessels, an overly thick heart, and stroke risk.

segments.title: Pre-hypertension, hypertension and white coat hypertension
segments.summary: The hosts distinguish pre-hypertension, which diet can correct, from secondary hypertension. They describe white coat hypertension, where blood pressure rises at the doctor's office, and note that blood pressure can be elevated during pregnancy.

segments.title: Prevalence statistics and risk factors
segments.summary: About thirty percent of adults over twenty have hypertension or take medication for it, with poor people at a higher rate than non-poor. Cheap packaged foods high in sodium are cited as a contributor.

segments.title: Prevention, smoking, DASH diet and medications
segments.summary: Advice includes eating healthy, losing weight, cutting salt, limiting alcohol and quitting smoking. Smoking is said to injure blood vessels. The DASH diet is recommended. Anti-hypertensive drug classes and their side effects are outlined, and the hosts say six in ten... (a claim that many hypertensive people recover control) is offered with hope.

segments.title: Visa sponsor read and frog extinction plug
segments.summary: Sponsor read for Visa on online fraud, followed by a plug for a how stuff works article about frogs as indicator species.
